verdict.root_cause: The payment path never broke. platform-automation set OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TRACES_ENDPOINT to a loopback address on paymentservice ~6 minutes before the 14:25:45 alert, the third application in a ~9h set/revert flap, touching no other key and no artifact [tr_7970c9cda487]. Spans stop arriving in the trace backend after ~14:17 despite a window extending to 14:27 [tr_79febd00f80b], while the process itself keeps serving successful sub-millisecond charges from one unchanged pid through 14:27:32 with no errors or restarts [tr_f60a43a23791], and caller checkoutservice shows a flat-zero error ratio across all 128 samples [tr_f7a92b0eca17]. The mechanism is a config value naming an address with no listener behind it: observability of paymentservice failed, not paymentservice.
verdict.reasoning: Logs, traces and the caller's error metric independently show paymentservice healthy at and after onset [tr_f60a43a23791][tr_79febd00f80b][tr_f7a92b0eca17], which eliminates crash, restart, exhaustion and in-handler latency. What is demonstrably missing is telemetry, and the only change in the window is a loopback OTLP endpoint applied six minutes prior [tr_7970c9cda487]. The wrong value is itself the failure, so config_revert (plus stopping the automation loop) is the fix. Confidence is medium because the trace specialist explicitly refused a clean cut-in at the change time - the last sampled span is 14:17:00, before the edit [tr_79febd00f80b] - and paymentservice metrics are absent in both incident and baseline windows [tr_bf5326f86bad], so that corroboration was never available.
open_questions: The last observed span predates the 14:19:42 edit by 2-3 minutes and only 6 of 34 traces were sampled [tr_79febd00f80b]; a per-minute span count would settle whether export ceased at the change or earlier.
The alert rule that fired at 14:25:45 was never retrieved, so whether it is an absence-of-telemetry alert is unconfirmed.

Traces flag shippingservice->quoteservice and frontend->checkout as degrading [tr_79febd00f80b]; neither service was dispatched and triage reports 2 unmeasured edges, so a concurrent latency problem is unexcluded.

alternatives.root_cause: Latency at the shippingservice->quoteservice hop in the checkout path is the real incident, with the paymentservice telemetry gap coincidental.
alternatives.why_not: Supported only by the trace sampler's hop attribution [tr_79febd00f80b]; nobody measured those services, and it does not explain a change landing six minutes before the alert.

alternatives.root_cause: paymentservice was never instrumented or scraped under that service label, so the alert reflects a pre-existing coverage gap rather than today's edit.
alternatives.why_not: Explains the empty metric series in both windows [tr_bf5326f86bad] but not the trace backend holding 34 paymentservice traces earlier in the same window that then stop [tr_79febd00f80b].

proposal.expected_effect: Restoring paymentservice's prior environment removes OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TRACES_ENDPOINT=http://127.0.0.1:4317, which was absent before the 14:19:42 edit [tr_7970c9cda487], so the exporter returns to its default collector and span export resumes. Observable as a trace query for paymentservice returning Charge spans with start times after the recreate, nested under checkoutservice as at 14:09-14:17 [tr_79febd00f80b]; equivalently a per-minute span count going from zero to non-zero. Logs should keep showing paired charge/transaction-complete info lines at sub-millisecond latency from a new pid [tr_f60a43a23791].
proposal.if_wrong: Falsified if, five minutes after the recreate, logs show charges served normally but trace queries over the post-revert window still return zero paymentservice spans - then export is broken by something else, consistent with the last span at ~14:17 predating the 14:19:42 edit [tr_79febd00f80b]. Also beside the point if the flagged frontend->checkout and shipping->quote degrading hops persist unchanged; a per-minute span count run first would settle this.
proposal.risk: The recreate drops in-flight Charge RPCs on a process evidence shows is healthy - same pid, no errors, sub-millisecond charges through 14:27:32 [tr_f60a43a23791]. Any payment failure in the next minutes is caused by this action. If the diagnosis is wrong, cost is a needless payment-path interruption plus false comfort while an unexcluded latency fault continues. platform-automation has flapped this key three times in ~9h [tr_7970c9cda487], so it will likely re-apply; do not loop this action.
proposal.blast_radius: paymentservice (container recreated, cache discarded); checkoutservice as immediate caller sees connection resets, a blip in its flat-zero error ratio; frontend and end users see failed or retried PlaceOrder during the recreate.

triage_judgement.reasoning: A critical alert on paymentservice sits upstream of checkout and frontend, so a real payment failure path cannot be dismissed. Single-service signal gives no fault-class hint yet.
